recognize_zh: 左下方有一個核偏位、胞質大量呈粉紫色的火焰細胞（flame cell），周圍卻是許多中型、核質比高、染色質細緻的芽細胞（blasts）；同一張圖同時看到異常漿細胞與大量芽細胞，需考慮骨髓瘤合併或併發急性骨髓性白血病。
features: Numerous medium-sized blasts with high N:C ratio, round to slightly irregular nuclei and fine dispersed chromatin
Blasts with scant basophilic agranular cytoplasm; Auer rods not seen
Single flame cell: plasma cell with eccentric dense nucleus and abundant magenta-pink cytoplasm
A few smaller mature lymphoid/erythroid cells nearby
Hemodilute background with clumped red cells
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows numerous medium-sized blasts with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, finely dispersed chromatin and scant basophilic agranular cytoplasm; Auer rods are not seen in this field. A single plasma cell with an eccentric dense nucleus and abundant magenta-pink cytoplasm (flame cell) is present among the blasts. Blast lineage cannot be established morphologically and requires flow cytometry. Findings are consistent with a flame cell in a marrow involved by acute leukemia, per the clinical description myeloblasts, raising concern for concurrent plasma cell neoplasm and AML (including therapy-related disease).

ddx.vs: Plasmablasts have eccentric nuclei with prominent nucleoli and more basophilic cytoplasm, and are CD138/clonal light chain-positive rather than CD34/MPO-positive.
Lymphoblasts can look identical morphologically; MPO cytochemistry and flow cytometry are required to assign lineage.

ddx.dx: Reactive plasma cell with flame morphology
ddx.vs: A single flame cell may be reactive; clonality by kappa/lambda and quantitation of plasma cells determine a neoplastic process.
